Review Make?

Reviewers largely see Make as an intuitive, flexible automation tool that lets non-technical teams build useful workflows quickly, while still handling fairly complex scenarios, branching, testing, scheduling, and custom app needs. Many use it for real operational work, from CRM and form routing to contract generation, BI syncing, and even MVP building. The main complaints are uneven reliability, debugging and error handling, occasional missing integrations or weak repeat logic, per-operation costs at scale, and inconsistent support. One founder from Boost.space also describes it as an orchestration engine for its own plans.

A tool that takes you from idea to DONE super quick. I had the opportunity to create a couple of trainings with Creatium and all of them were built from some ideas that I had sitting but had never had time to implement. With the tool, I was able to specifiy outcomes, provide something items that were important to me, and watch teh system do the rest. Literally within a day, I had a working working training that I could share with the team. Even with how quickly it worked, I was able to modidy and make the changes I needed to put in knowedlge checks and even a game into the learning workflow. Perfect if you have training outlines you've been dying to execute on but no time or budget to create training the old-fashioned way.

Review Creatium?

Reviewers consistently describe Creatium as intuitive, fast, and genuinely useful for building training from rough ideas. They say it helps teams create working courses quickly, customize outcomes, add knowledge checks, games, simulations, avatars, and even language changes, while making the experience feel interactive and coach-like. Several reviews point to strong use in staff training, especially for practice-heavy scenarios like difficult conversations. Support and responsiveness are praised throughout. The feedback is notably one-sided, with no meaningful criticism or tradeoffs mentioned.
